# Developer tooling and repo housekeeping {#sec-housekeeping}

- The work that keeps the repository, the website and the developer
  experience in order. Grouping labels: `documentation`, `refactor`.
- Like the test suite (@sec-test-suite), this is ongoing work that
  earns a milestone now that milestones no longer imply a version. It
  is the natural filler for a patch release.

**What is in here.** Four strands, none of which blocks any other.

*Repository and tooling*:
[#716](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/716) (get the linter
working again), [#368](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/368)
(use `lifecycle` for deprecation, which the plan will need as soon as
the two breaking changes in milestone 8 land),
[#721](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/721) (tell GitHub this
is an R repository, not C++), and
[#803](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/803) (documenting the
internal R6 classes).

*Documentation mechanics*:
[#442](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/442) (`@examplesIf`),
[#724](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/724) (roxygen `family`
tags), [#768](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/768) (use the
penguins data in examples), plus two content items -
[#505](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/505) (more prediction
examples) and [#571](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/571)
(non-independent sampling with `greta_array()`).

*The website and blog*:
[#435](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/435) and
[#822](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/822) (the blog, now
built and awaiting the 0.6.0 post being proofed and un-drafted),
[#623](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/623) (a papers-using-greta
page), and [#812](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/812) (the
dead `greta-stats.org` apex domain). [#812](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/812) is the only item in this
milestone that needs an account action rather than a commit, and it is
not greta's account: the domain belongs to Nick Golding.

*The umbrella trackers*:
[#322](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/322) (the 2020 coding
sprint plan) and [#744](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/744)
(revisit the TODO list). Both are kept open by policy rather than
because they describe work - [#322](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/322)'s sub-items have all been rehomed
into the milestones, and [#744](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/744) is circular by construction. They are
here so that the tracker has somewhere honest to put them.

## [Issue #368](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/368)

- 2021-04-12
- (none)

## [Issue #435](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/435)

- 2021-07-08
- documentation
- Add a blog to the website.
- finding: greta.blog is being revived (July 2026) as a modern Quarto site.
- fix: no package code - link the revived greta.blog from the pkgdown `_pkgdown.yml` navbar and the README, seed it with one release/forum-derived post, then close in favour of it. ## [Issue #812](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/812)

- 2026-07-07
- (none)
- Resolve the greta-stats.org website/DNS issue.
- **rescoped: this is a cross-repo URL sweep, not only a DNS task.** `greta-stats.org` is dead, not merely misconfigured — it fails with `SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches`. `https://greta-dev.github.io/greta/` returns 200 and is the live site. The dead domain is still linked from **greta (7 files), greta.distributions (3), greta.dynamics (2), greta.gp (1)**, and `index.qmd` of this book (now fixed). Either restore the domain *or* sweep every reference to the GitHub Pages URL — the current state is both half-done. Add a URL check to CI so it cannot recur.
- problem: needs direct action on Netlify/DNS access, plus edits in four repos.
- finding: the one item requiring an account action as well as code.
- fix: no package code - an infrastructure action for the domain owner (`@goldingn`): the stale A record points `greta-stats.org` at an old AWS Sydney IP so Netlify never provisioned a Let's Encrypt cert (hostname/TLS mismatch, HTTPS hard-fails). Verify the custom domain on the Netlify site and repoint DNS to Netlify's endpoint (or migrate DNS/hosting to GitHub Pages as done for njtierney.com). Acceptance: `https://greta-stats.org` serves a valid cert with no hostname mismatch. Blocks [#435](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/435) (blog link) and [#623](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/623) (papers page) being reachable; no code dependency.
- priority: high (public-facing), small.

::: {.callout-note}
## Partly overtaken, July 2026

Only the apex domain is dead. `https://forum.greta-stats.org` returns 200, so
the forum links in greta's pkgdown navbar and in the blog footer are fine — the
sweep is narrower than the block above implies. The blog itself
([#435](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/435),
[#822](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/822)) is now built and linked
from the greta website, so it is no longer blocked on this.
:::
## [Issue #822](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/822)

- 2026-07-21
- low hanging fruit
- Establish the greta blog.
- problem: a checklist issue - stand up pkgdown on the blog, proofread the existing posts, proofread and publish the 0.6.0 release post, and share it.
- finding: partly done. The blog is built and linked from the greta website, which also retires the old dependency on the dead `greta-stats.org` apex domain (see [#812](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/812)). What remains is editorial: the 0.6.0 announcement post is written but still carries `draft: true` and a TODO-verify marker on its contributor list.
- fix: proofread the drafted 0.6.0 post, verify the contributor list against the actual release, drop `draft: true`, publish, and announce. Closes alongside [#435](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/435), which asked for the blog component in the first place.
- priority: medium, and entirely editorial - no package code.
